notes: Hosts that commonly answer automated requests with 403, 405 or 429 (bot protection, login walls, paywalls). check-links.ts treats a 403, 405 or 429 from these hosts as a warning instead of a failure, and so is any answer other than 404 or 410 that carries a bot challenge header (challengeHeaders: Cloudflare's cf-mitigated, Vercel's x-vercel-mitigated, AWS WAF's x-amzn-waf-action), because the real page was not seen. A host matches itself and its subdomains. expectedMissing lists URLs cited as evidence that a page is gone (a 404 or 410 there is the expected answer). expectedStatus maps URLs to another documented answer, such as an x402 endpoint that answers 402 or a site whose hosting answers 402 and whose source record says so.
